Eddie Pack did the quarter but did not extend himself, and the Ealing man gained slightly, but Les Bennett and Alec Mewes, our two sprinters, kept our lead to win a good race.

The 220 yards was won by Stan Blunden off 8 yards, with Dick Michael (12) second, and Alec Mewes (11) third. Blunden is another runner to show remarkable improvement this season and if he can only improve his rather ungainly style he should still further increase his speed.
Pritchard and Tom Wiley—finishing in that order—gave us a close race. Eddie Pack, Alec Mewes, S. Lyons and Les Bennett gained Standards (24 sec.) in their heats.

Alec Mewes, we understand, is home on leave from the M.E.F. Alec is on our list of lost contacts, so can anybody furnish particulars of his presesnt whereabouts please.
We announce with deepest regret the following death:— Alec Mewes was killed in France. He was 29 years old and joined us in 1928 when only 13 years old.

In addition, there were PAT RIDGE and FRANK HANDLEY (both of the Irish Guards) killed in action, as were two other most promising athletes, K.N. WOOD (Lt.RA) and ALEC MEWES. There were many others also who laid down their lives in 1939-1945.
